tagline: Turn any website into clean, LLM-ready data
description_md:
**Firecrawl** turns any website into clean, LLM-ready data. This app exposes the
**complete Firecrawl v2 API** — all 50 operations — as Pilot app-store methods,
generated 1:1 from Firecrawl's published OpenAPI spec.

**Run `firecrawl.signup` once.** It provisions a real mailbox for your Pilot identity,
registers it with Firecrawl, and caches the returned API key locally — no email to
supply, no browser, no human step. From then on every method authenticates
automatically against **your own Firecrawl account**: your own 10,000 credits, your own
rate and concurrency limits, your own jobs. Nothing is shared with other Pilot users.

Calling `firecrawl.signup` accepts [Firecrawl's Terms of
Service](https://www.firecrawl.dev/terms-of-service); the acceptance is recorded against
your Pilot identity with a timestamp, and `firecrawl.account` shows it back to you.

**What you get**

- **Scrape** — one URL to clean markdown, HTML, links, screenshots, or schema-shaped
  JSON. Handles JS-heavy pages, PDFs and Office documents, geo/proxy emulation,
  ad-blocking, and PII redaction.
- **Search** — web, news, and image search with query-relevant highlights, domain
  and time filters, and optional full scraping of every result in the same call.
- **Map** — enumerate every URL on a domain in about a second. The cheap way to scope
  a crawl before you pay for one.
- **Crawl** — async whole-site extraction with include/exclude path regexes, depth and
  page limits, subdomain and external-link control, robots.txt handling, and webhooks.
  Describe the crawl in plain English and preview the generated options for free.
- **Batch scrape** — many known URLs in one job, with per-URL error reporting.
- **Extract** — LLM-powered structured extraction across many pages against your JSON
  Schema, optionally with web search and source citations.
- **Agent** — autonomous web research. Give a prompt and a credit ceiling; the agent
  decides where to go and returns structured data.
- **Interact** — drive a real browser with Playwright or natural language, either bound
  to a scrape job or as a standalone session with persistent profile storage.
- **Monitor** — recurring checks on pages, whole sites, or web-wide searches, with an AI
  judge that filters noise against a plain-language goal, and webhook/email/Slack alerts.
- **Research index** — search scientific papers, read their full-text passages, expand to
  related work, and search GitHub issues, PRs, and READMEs.
- **Support** — `firecrawl.ask` diagnoses a failing job from your account's logs, and
  `firecrawl.docs_search` answers Firecrawl questions with citations.
- **Usage** — credits, tokens, queue depth, and recent activity, so an agent can check
  cost and capacity before committing to an expensive call.

**Start with `firecrawl.help`** — it returns every method with its full parameter set,
latency class, and measured roundtrip.

**Cost control.** `firecrawl.crawl` takes `limit` and `firecrawl.agent` takes
`maxCredits`; both default high. Set them — a crawl bills per page. `firecrawl.map` and
`firecrawl.crawl_params_preview` are the cheap ways to scope work before you spend.
Check `firecrawl.credit_usage` before a large job. Your starting credits expire 3 months
after signup and are granted once per identity.

**Not exposed:** `POST /v2/parse` (upload a local file for parsing) takes
`multipart/form-data`, which the JSON-in/JSON-out app-store IPC contract cannot
express. Use `firecrawl.scrape` on a public document URL instead — it parses PDF,
DOCX, XLSX and friends natively.

methods.name: firecrawl.signup
methods.summary: Get your OWN Firecrawl account and API key in one call — no email, no browser, no human step. Provisions a real mailbox for your Pilot identity, registers it with Firecrawl, and caches the returned key so every other firecrawl.* method authenticates automatically. Idempotent: one account per Pilot identity, so a repeat call returns the same one. You get your own credit balance and your own concurrency limit — nothing is shared with other Pilot users. BY CALLING THIS YOU ACCEPT FIRECRAWL'S TERMS OF SERVICE (https://www.firecrawl.dev/terms-of-service); the acceptance is recorded against your Pilot identity with a timestamp. Run it ONCE before anything else.

methods.name: firecrawl.account
methods.summary: Show your Firecrawl account — the mailbox provisioned for you, a signed_up flag, and when you accepted Firecrawl's terms. Local, instant, free (reads $APP/secrets.json; no backend call). If signed_up is false, call firecrawl.signup first.

methods.name: firecrawl.scrape
methods.summary: Scrape one URL into clean LLM-ready markdown (or html/links/screenshot/json).

methods.name: firecrawl.scrape_status
methods.summary: Get the status and result of a previously started scrape job by id.

methods.name: firecrawl.scrape_interact
methods.summary: Run code or an AI prompt in the live browser session bound to a scrape job.

methods.name: firecrawl.scrape_interact_stop
methods.summary: Stop the interactive browser session attached to a scrape job and free its resources.

methods.name: firecrawl.search
methods.summary: Search the web (and optionally scrape every result in one call).

methods.name: firecrawl.search_feedback
methods.summary: Rate a search job's quality to improve future Firecrawl search results.

methods.name: firecrawl.map
methods.summary: Discover every URL on a domain, fast — the cheap way to scope a crawl.

methods.name: firecrawl.crawl
methods.summary: Start an async crawl of an entire site. Returns a job id — poll firecrawl.crawl_status.

methods.name: firecrawl.crawl_status
methods.summary: Poll a crawl job: status, completed/total counts, credits used, and the scraped pages.

methods.name: firecrawl.crawl_cancel
methods.summary: Cancel a running crawl job.

methods.name: firecrawl.crawl_errors
methods.summary: List the pages a crawl job failed on, plus URLs blocked by robots.txt.

methods.name: firecrawl.crawl_active
methods.summary: List every crawl currently running for your account.

methods.name: firecrawl.crawl_params_preview
methods.summary: Dry-run: see the crawl options a natural-language prompt would generate, without spending credits.

methods.name: firecrawl.batch_scrape
methods.summary: Scrape many known URLs in one async job. Returns a job id — poll firecrawl.batch_scrape_status.

methods.name: firecrawl.batch_scrape_status
methods.summary: Poll a batch scrape job: progress, credits used, and the scraped pages.

methods.name: firecrawl.batch_scrape_cancel
methods.summary: Cancel a running batch scrape job.

methods.name: firecrawl.batch_scrape_errors
methods.summary: List the URLs a batch scrape job failed on, with per-URL error detail.

methods.name: firecrawl.extract
methods.summary: Extract structured JSON from one or many pages using an LLM and your schema. Async — poll firecrawl.extract_status.

methods.name: firecrawl.extract_status
methods.summary: Poll an extract job and retrieve the structured data once it completes.

methods.name: firecrawl.agent
methods.summary: Autonomous web research: give a prompt, the agent decides what to visit and returns structured data. Async — poll firecrawl.agent_status.

methods.name: firecrawl.agent_status
methods.summary: Poll an agent job and retrieve its result once it completes.

methods.name: firecrawl.agent_cancel
methods.summary: Cancel a running agent job and stop it spending credits.

methods.name: firecrawl.interact_create
methods.summary: Start a standalone browser session you drive with code — no prior scrape needed.

methods.name: firecrawl.interact_list
methods.summary: List your standalone interact browser sessions.

methods.name: firecrawl.interact_execute
methods.summary: Run Playwright or agent-browser code inside a standalone interact session.

methods.name: firecrawl.interact_delete
methods.summary: Destroy a standalone interact session and release its browser.

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_create
methods.summary: Create a recurring check that watches pages, a whole site, or search results and alerts on meaningful change.

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_list
methods.summary: List your monitors.

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_get
methods.summary: Get one monitor's full configuration.

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_update
methods.summary: Update a monitor's schedule, targets, goal, or status (active/paused).

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_delete
methods.summary: Delete a monitor and stop its recurring checks.

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_run
methods.summary: Trigger a monitor check immediately instead of waiting for its schedule.

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_checks
methods.summary: List a monitor's past checks and what changed in each.

methods.name: firecrawl.monitor_check
methods.summary: Get one monitor check in full, with page-level diffs.

methods.name: firecrawl.research_papers
methods.summary: Search a purpose-built scientific paper index by natural-language query.

methods.name: firecrawl.research_paper
methods.summary: Inspect a paper's metadata, or pass query to read its top matching full-text passages.

methods.name: firecrawl.research_related
methods.summary: Expand a seed paper to related work — citers, references, or semantically similar papers.

methods.name: firecrawl.research_github
methods.summary: Search GitHub issues, pull requests, discussions, and READMEs by natural-language query.

methods.name: firecrawl.ask
methods.summary: Diagnose a failing Firecrawl call with an AI support agent — pass the jobId and get a fix.

methods.name: firecrawl.docs_search
methods.summary: Answer a "how does Firecrawl do X?" question from the official docs, with citations.

methods.name: firecrawl.feedback
methods.summary: Submit quality feedback for a completed search, scrape, parse, or map job.

methods.name: firecrawl.credit_usage
methods.summary: Remaining credits and the current billing period.

methods.name: firecrawl.credit_usage_historical
methods.summary: Historical credit usage over time, optionally broken down by API key.

methods.name: firecrawl.token_usage
methods.summary: Remaining LLM tokens for extract-family operations.

methods.name: firecrawl.token_usage_historical
methods.summary: Historical token usage over time, optionally broken down by API key.

methods.name: firecrawl.queue_status
methods.summary: Your scrape queue depth, active jobs, and max concurrency — check before a large batch.

methods.name: firecrawl.activity
methods.summary: Recent API activity (last 24h) with job ids you can feed to the *_status methods.

methods.name: firecrawl.threat_protection
methods.summary: Read the account's threat-protection policy (URL risk checks, allow/deny lists).

methods.name: firecrawl.threat_protection_update
methods.summary: Replace the account's threat-protection policy. Full-document update — unspecified fields reset to defaults.

methods.name: firecrawl.help
methods.summary: Discovery: every method with params, kind, and latency class.
